title: a capture typed at a class built from text converts where the match crosses into the program, and a segment that class refuses is a `400`
scope:
where a route capture declared at a class implementing `Parses` runs that class's `parse`,
and what a segment it refuses becomes. Not the `#[Query]` half of
`rule:routing/a-bad-query-value-is-a-400`, which still binds nothing; not the command-argument half,
which `nvs_runtime::commands::ArgConv::Parses` already settled.
dependsOnText:
[0077](0077.md) and [0102](0102.md) for the capture's type list and the `404`,
[0024](0024.md) for what a converted capture carries, [0066](0066.md) for the `parse`/`tryParse` pair
the interface encodes.

summary.headline: A route capture typed at your own class converts in the handler, or is a 400
summary.body:
The router narrows a path segment on the types it reads natively: `int`, `uint`, `decimal`,
`Core\Uuid` and a few more. A segment one of those refuses is not a match, and the walk
continues toward a 404. A capture declared at any other class that parses from text matches on
shape only; the class's own `parse` runs where the handler reads the value, so no user code runs
on URLs that matched nothing. A segment the class then refuses throws over a route that did
match, which is a 400, like a bad query value.
